doc_verification.detail: ActivityStatus enum documented as uppercase (HOT). Lowercase 'hot' is legacy alias mapped to ACTIVE. Correctly rejected but with Type2 diagnosis.

execution_evidence.log_pattern: c1: POST /schema/{className}/tenants with activityStatus='hot' (lowercase) → HTTP 422, error: 'activityStatus in body should be one of [ACTIVE INACTIVE OFFLOADED OFFLOADING ONLOADING HOT COLD FROZEN FREEZING UNFREEZING]'

http_semantics.note: Correct rejection (case-sensitive enum), Type2: no explicit 'case-sensitive' hint

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: activityStatus enum: [ACTIVE, INACTIVE, OFFLOADED, OFFLOADING, ONLOADING, HOT, COLD, FROZEN, FREEZING, UNFREEZING]

chain_links: doc: OpenAPI spec shows HOT as valid value
log: HTTP 422 with enum list (correct rejection, Type2 diagnosis)

source_grounding.source_excerpt: Line 102-107 shows validateActivityStatusEnum calling validate.EnumCase with third parameter 'true' (case-insensitive flag). However, enum array only contains uppercase values, so lowercase 'hot' fails enum membership check despite being documented legacy alias.
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Tenant.Validate() → validateActivityStatus() → validateActivityStatusEnum() → EnumCase(check, case-insensitive) → rejection
